  PROBLEM: `_find_pr_merge_commit_for_path` uses `git log --grep=#{pr_str}\b -E`, which is brittle across merge-subject formats and regex implementations.

- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:~830-870 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The merge-commit lookup assumes a narrow squash-merge subject format via `--grep=#{pr_str}\b`, so valid merge commits can be missed.
  WHY: When the lookup fails, the verifier-side defense is disabled for those commits.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:299-362 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `git log --grep` regex can exhibit pathological backtracking on very long commit messages.
  WHY: Cache-miss lookups can consume significant CPU up to the command timeout before the cache warms.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:~830-910 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new defense only checks `must_not_contain` patterns and never evaluates the symmetric partial-add case for `must_contain`.
  WHY: Asymmetric handling can misclassify partial adds or let regressions slip.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3065-3078 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The quiet `git fetch` fallback swallows resolve/fetch errors and silently falls back to local state.
  WHY: Operators cannot tell whether the post-merge filter ran, and stale state may be used.
- tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_partial_removal.py:~470-490 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The heredoc extractor is brittle string-index parsing of the shell script.
  WHY: Small refactors can break the test or make it validate stale heredoc content.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:289-450 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new private helpers/caches are introduced without a versioning or deprecation guard.
  WHY: Downstream consumers or future refactors can break tests or scripts that start depending on the new symbols.
